verdict.rationale: Highnote's agentic-commerce docs describe issuing per-agent payment cards via API with velocity limits, MCC restrictions, per-transaction caps, and automatic closure when a workflow ends — a form of scoped, least-privilege credentialing tailored to agents (highnote-docs-17, 18, 21). However, the evidence is entirely first-party marketing/docs with no independent or hands-on verification, and it doesn't address whether the underlying API keys/auth tokens themselves support granular scoping (docs-26 even suggests a single API key/endpoint model). Missing for 10: independent corroboration, documentation of API-key-level (not just card-level) permission scoping, and real-world examples of least-privilege enforcement.
